title: Health & the Doctor
description: Symptoms, medicine and the clinic: words for telling a doctor or a pharmacist what's wrong, and for understanding what they tell you.

items.registerNotes: Batuk kering is a dry cough and batuk berdahak a chesty one; obat batuk is cough medicine.
Saya pilek (I've got a cold). A blocked nose is hidung tersumbat.

items.pitfallNote: Indonesians use flu for an ordinary cold with a runny nose too, so kena flu (to come down with the flu) may mean less than it sounds.

items.cultureNote: Literally wind getting in, and blamed on rain, night air or a fan: aches, bloating and tiredness. The home cure is kerokan, scraping the back with a coin and oil, which leaves red stripes.

items.registerNotes: Sakit plus a body part names the pain: sakit gigi (toothache), sakit tenggorokan (sore throat).
items.pitfallNote: Pusing means dizzy but is often used for a headache too; sakit kepala is the clear word for a pain in the head.

items.registerNotes: Perut is the stomach or belly. Mulas is the cramping feeling that sends you to the toilet.
The neutral word for doctors and pharmacies; mencret is blunt and casual. Oralit (oral rehydration salts) is sold at every apotek.
Saya mual (I feel sick). Seasickness is mabuk laut, though mabuk on its own means drunk.
The plain word, fine with a doctor: Saya muntah dua kali (I've thrown up twice).
Terluka means injured, and luka bakar is a burn. A graze from a scooter fall is lecet.
Gatal-gatal is an itchy rash, and a mosquito bite is gigitan nyamuk.

items.pitfallNote: No word for to: Saya alergi udang (I'm allergic to prawns). Kacang covers peanuts, nuts and beans, so say kacang tanah for peanuts.
The same word means a recipe, so context decides. Obat resep needs a prescription; obat bebas is sold over the counter.

items.cultureNote: For everyday illness people go to a klinik or the local puskesmas (community health centre), not straight to a hospital.

items.registerNotes: Female nurses are usually addressed as Suster or Sus, male ones as Mas. Rawat inap is a hospital stay, rawat jalan outpatient care.
Disuntik is to get an injection: Perlu disuntik? (Do I need an injection?) A vaccination is suntik vaksin or vaksinasi.

items.cultureNote: Clinics usually check it first, whatever you've come for: Cek tensi dulu, ya. Tekanan darah is the formal term.

items.registerNotes: Periksa ke dokter is to see a doctor, and diperiksa is being examined. Memeriksa is the written form; cek is common in speech.

items.english: to rest; a rest, a break
items.registerNotes: Doctors say Banyak istirahat, ya (Get plenty of rest). Jam istirahat is a lunch break or break time.

items.cultureNote: Semoga cepat sembuh (Get well soon) is what everyone says to someone who's ill, in person or by message.

items.registerNotes: For a known condition coming back: Maag saya kambuh (My gastritis is back) is a complaint you'll hear often.

items.pitfallNote: You drink medicine in Indonesian, even pills: minum obat. Instructions sound like tiga kali sehari satu tablet (one tablet three times a day).

items.registerNotes: Obat sirup is liquid medicine, measured with a sendok takar (measuring spoon). Sirup is also the sweet cordial served to guests, especially at Lebaran.
items.pitfallNote: Dictionaries spell it sirop, but labels, pharmacies and nearly everyone write and say sirup.

items.registerNotes: Labels say Oleskan tipis-tipis (Apply a thin layer).
Sakit gigi is toothache and dokter gigi a dentist; sikat gigi is both a toothbrush and to brush your teeth.
Sakit mata is sore or infected eyes, and obat tetes mata is eye drops. Mata turns up in other words too: matahari (sun), mata uang (currency).
